subject: Private deployment: customer KMS responsibilities & DPA / subprocessors
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-cloudware.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-09-01 09:12 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: KMS responsibilities / DPA questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this - we're evaluating Redwood for a private (VPC / on-prem) deployment and have a handful of privacy and subprocessor questions to resolve before procurement can sign off. High level: we need assurance that when we run Redwood inside our environment or VPC, our customers' plaintext and model inputs are only ever accessible to our systems, and that key custody remains under our control. Specific asks below: 

- Can Redwood confirm support for customer-managed KMS for both VPC-managed and on-prem installs? Do you provide a key-rotation / escrow mechanism?
- Under what circumstances (if any) would Redwood personnel be able to decrypt customer data or access KV cache? Any emergency access / break-glass process?
- Please provide your current list of subprocessors that may have any role touching private deployments (including install partners). We specifically need names, roles, regions, and whether they have access to encrypted backups.
- Cross‑border transfer question: if Redwood needs to receive any telemetry or logs for Private deployments, how is PII handled and where is it transmitted?
- Can we get your SOC2 report and the latest DPA (we've attached our security questionnaire and target DPA clauses for your review).

Our legal counsel (cc'd later) may follow with redline requests; happy to set a 30-minute sync to go through the DPA and subprocessors list.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Infrastructure Security
Acme Cloudware

Attachment: ACME_Security_Questionnaire_2025.pdf

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-cloudware.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-09-01 10:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: KMS responsibilities / DPA questions

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, then a proposed next step: 30-minute call early next week to walk through the redline.

- Customer-managed KMS: yes. For Private deployments (both VPC and on‑prem), we support customer‑provided KMS (Cloud KMS or HSM) with full key-on-host options where Redwood does not hold key material.
- Key rotation / escrow: Redwood can integrate with customer KMS rotation policies. We do not require escrow by default; if you request an emergency key‑escrow arrangement, that needs to be explicitly scoped in the MSA addendum and will include two-party approvals and audit trails.
- Personnel access: By default, Redwood personnel do not have access to plaintext in on‑prem or customer‑KMS-backed VPC deployments. We can include contractual language stating that Redwood has no operational capability to decrypt customer inputs unless an agreed exception process is followed (see below).
- Subprocessors: for Private installs the list is intentionally small — installer partners and (rare) hardware vendors. For Hosted/Managed we use cloud infra providers and telemetry processors. I've attached our current DPA draft (v3) and the subprocessors manifest for your review.
- Telemetry/logs: We recommend a default of keeping telemetry within the customer VPC or pointing telemetry to customer-managed endpoints. If any minimal telemetry is sent to Redwood for health/metrics, it will be pseudonymized and agreed in the DPA.

I've attached: DPA_Draft_v3.pdf and subprocessors_manifest_2025.csv. Proposed next step: 09/03 or 09/04 for a 30-min call with our infra/legal owners.

—Kimberly Park
Head of Legal (Commercial & Security)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Draft_v3.pdf, subprocessors_manifest_2025.csv

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-09-02 08:30 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment: KMS responsibilities / DPA questions — internal notes

Kim / Rishi —

Quick internal notes before we sync with Acme:

1) DPA redline suggestions (I attached a tracked-change summary to the Drive link):
   - Add explicit "no access" clause for plaintext in on‑prem and customer‑KMS-backed VPC installs (include operational proof: attestations + recent supply chain audit date).
   - Define emergency access narrowly: require (a) written request from authorized ACME security lead, (b) two Redwood approvals (Legal + CTO), (c) preserved audit logs, (d) time-limited access and proof of deletion.
2) Subprocessor constraints: add a table in the DPA listing allowed installer partners and the onboarding checklist (background checks, region-limited access). For hosted customers we keep the standard list, but for Private deployments default to "no third-party access to encrypted payloads."
3) Telemetry: default to customer-forwarding; only aggregate metrics to Redwood unless customer opts in.

Also flagging that ACME asked explicitly about backups — ensure clause that encrypted backups remain customer-controlled; no Redwood ability to restore unless keys are provided by ACME under the emergency process.

I'll prepare a short set of bullet edits to propose on the call.

Marissa
Director, Product Security (Redwood)

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-cloudware.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Patrick Owen <patrick.owen@lawfirm-evans.com>
Date: 2025-09-03 11:15 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: KMS responsibilities / DPA questions

Kimberly / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick responses and the attachments; we received DPA_Draft_v3.pdf and subprocessors_manifest_2025.csv. A few clarifying follow-ups before the sync: 

- Does Redwood require any form of key escrow for on‑prem installs as a default? Your note implies optional; our security policy prefers no escrow.
- Can you confirm that Redwood will not be able to access encrypted backups OR KV cache unless the customer explicitly grants a key? Please confirm that this is a technical limitation (i.e., no secret-share or escrow inside the installer).
- Cross‑border: if Redwood must receive telemetry, what countries might logs transit through? We are EU/US hybrid and need assurance no EU personal data is routed to a non‑approved jurisdiction.

I've looped our counsel, Patrick Owen, who will drive the DPA redlines. Patrick — attaching our short DPA summary that lists must-have clauses.

Propose a 30-minute call Friday 09/05 at 10:00 AM PT if that works for you.

Elena

Attachment: ACME_DPA_Summary.pdf

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-cloudware.com>, Patrick Owen <patrick.owen@lawfirm-evans.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-09-04 09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: KMS responsibilities / DPA questions — commitments & next steps

Elena / Patrick —

Thanks — appreciate the diligence. Confirming Redwood's commitments for Acme Cloudware's Private deployment (to be reflected in the DPA addendum):

1) Key custody: Acme retains exclusive custody of KMS keys for customer-KMS configurations. Redwood will integrate with customer KMS APIs for wrapping/unwrapping per agreed flows but will not persist key material. No default escrow. Any escrow/restore arrangement is optional and requires a separate signed addendum.

2) Plaintext and KV cache access: Redwood engineering and ops will not have access to customer plaintext, model inputs, or KV caches in on‑prem or customer‑KMS VPC installs. The installer is designed such that decryption requires customer-held keys.

3) Emergency access: we will propose a narrowly-scoped exception process in the DPA addendum: written request from an authorized Acme representative, two Redwood approvers (Legal + CTO), time-limited access with forensics, and documented deletion/rollback steps. All actions will be logged and made available to Acme on request.

4) Backups: encrypted backups remain under Acme control. Redwood will only be able to restore if Acme provides key material or explicit authorization per the emergency process.

5) Subprocessors: for Private deployments, subprocessors are limited to the named installer partner and approved hardware vendors listed in subprocessors_manifest_2025.csv. Any onboarding of additional subprocessors that could access encrypted payloads requires prior written consent.

6) Telemetry & cross-border: default behavior is to keep telemetry inside Acme's VPC endpoints. If Acme elects to send aggregate telemetry to Redwood, Redwood will ensure pseudonymization and will provide a transfer impact assessment. We will commit to routing telemetry through US or EU regions only as requested in the DPA.

Next steps:
- I've uploaded a redline DPA with the addendum language to the Drive link.
- Proposed DocuSign pre-fill for signature: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/ACM-2025-045.
- We'll hold the 30-min sync on 2025-09-05 10:00 AM PT to walk through the redline (Marissa and Rishi will join).

If that covers your primary points, we'll push the DPA redline to DocuSign after the call and follow with the MSA addendum if you want escrow options.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal (Commercial & Security)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Draft_v3_redline.pdf
